facts.text: Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
The party holds a treasure map marking several locations they do not recognize, near Brandonsford.

classification.support_basis: The map is the party's only guide to the treasure, though they cannot yet match its marked locations to the land.

facts.text: Where is the treasure the map marks?

classification.grounding_justification: The beat explicitly states the map's locations are unrecognized and the party only assumes the treasure is in one of them.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering it means matching the map's marks to unknown land, mostly a location-finding task.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Finding where the treasure lies is mainly instrumental to recovering it.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party can ask locals and explore the surrounding land to identify the marked locations.

facts.text: Reginald the Frog says a little trickster creature called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away wherever it goes.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Reginald only says the creature is up to no good and to stay away; no specific harm is named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: It is described as a little trickster, suggesting mischief rather than serious harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on a single frog's testimony that the creature comes every night.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald describes a nightly recurring pattern of the creature entering town.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can heed the warning and avoid where it goes, though no means to stop it is established.

facts.text: What does the Clurichen do when it comes into town each night?

classification.grounding_justification: Reginald's warning that the creature is up to no good nightly clearly raises what it is doing, without framing it conspicuously.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the creature's hidden nightly activity and intention.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning its mischief could explain strange events in town, but nothing in the record ties it to any yet.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could watch the riverbanks or town at night to follow it.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon troubling Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
George, a woodsman living a couple of houses from the Clumsy Fox who may come to the tavern tonight, met the dragon and lost an arm to it; the party could question him about the dragon.

classification.support_basis: George is the only known eyewitness who fought the dragon and could tell where he met it and what it can do, though he has only described it as a small black dragon so far.
classification.action_basis: Eric pointed the party to George's house and said he may come to the tavern tonight, so the party can find and question him.

facts.text: Lady Hilda would join the party against the dragon for pay (see her offer's thread).

classification.support_basis: A seasoned, armoured fighter would strengthen the party against the dragon.
classification.action_basis: Lady Hilda offered to join a party of adventurers for money in the context of the dragon.

facts.resource_subject: Lady Hilda's offer to join the party for pay

facts.text: Where is the black dragon to be found?

classification.grounding_justification: The dragon has been seen around town by George and Gill, and Gill's sons are hunting it, but nobody has said where it lairs.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Finding a location is a straightforward discovery.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Witnesses like George, Gill and his sons and tracking in the wilds offer leads to follow.

facts.text: Where has this new dragon come from, centuries after Sir Brandon killed the first?

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley says nothing like this has happened since Sir Brandon's dragon, and Gill says the old one was definitely dead and he doesn't know where dragons come from.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the circumstance behind the dragon's appearance.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: It could explain the town's sudden trouble and connect to its founding legend.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Local legend and the dragon's tracks could be followed, though no specific lead exists.

facts.text: The black dragon, which tore off George the woodsman's arm, is still at large around Brandonsford and may maim others.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: George's lost arm shows the specific harm: maiming of those who meet it.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Eric reports George's encounter and Gill saw the dragon himself.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: It remains near town and Gill's sons are hunting it, but no pattern of repeated attacks is shown; Gill says it wanted nothing to do with him.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing the dragon, as the bounty asks, would end it.

facts.text: Farmer Gill's three sons are hunting the dragon now and could kill it before the party, taking the Reeve's bounty.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The specific loss is the party missing the bounty if another kills the dragon first.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Loss of the reward, not physical harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Gill states his sons are hunting it, but nothing says they can succeed.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The hunt is underway now, but no progress toward a kill is shown.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could hunt the dragon promptly or work with the sons.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned fighter in chain mail with a shield, offers to join the party against the dragon for pay.

classification.support_basis: A fighter who looks more seasoned than the party would add real strength to an attempt to kill the dragon for the Reeve's bounty, though her fee is unset.
classification.action_basis: Lady Hilda explicitly offered to join a party of adventurers against the dragon for money; the party can return to the Clumsy Fox and hire her.

facts.resource_subject: Lady Hilda's offer to join the party for pay

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk to the Reeve and then come back to take up her services.

classification.stake_basis: Sir Phidipaldi only stated the party's intention; nothing shows Lady Hilda relies on their return beyond a general interest in paid work.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned, a thief with a killer wasp in a jar, offers himself and the wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, doing anything as long as he gets to kill people; Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

classification.support_basis: A hired killer with a fast-killing wasp could add fighting strength against the dragon the party could kill for the Reeve's bounty, though Ned's interest is in killing people and no one has linked him to the dragon.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered his services at 100 gold a week, and hiring him would add a capable killer to the party.

facts.text: Why has nothing come into Brandonsford in months, including Bentley's restock shipment that was due a week ago?

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley, Farmer Gill and Quinn all independently note that shipments have stopped for months, hurting the whole town, and Bentley calls it unprecedented since Sir Brandon's time; no cause is given.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal an underlying cause, such as an event or actor cutting off the town's supply.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Explaining a months-long, unprecedented supply failure would change the party's understanding of the town's troubles.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Townsfolk, merchants and the roads into town offer leads that could plausibly be followed.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi wants to fight Eric the Reeve in the duel he challenged him to at dawn.
Will Eric the Reeve, offended by Sir Phidipaldi, accept his challenge to a duel at dawn?

classification.grounding_justification: Sir Phidipaldi formally challenged Eric with a glove slap and Eric gave only a flustered non-answer, leaving the challenge conspicuously unresolved.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single fact about Eric's response settles it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting social consequence, mainly instrumental.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Answered simply by turning up at dawn or asking Eric.

facts.text: Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus, which Gill offers to sell for 100 gold.
When Dunk asked to trade work for Shamus, Farmer Gill said the big work needed is killing the dragon; he did not say outright he would give the mule for it.
facts.uncertain_reason: Gill named the dragon as the work needed but never explicitly agreed to trade Shamus for it.

classification.support_basis: Killing the dragon might let Dunk get Shamus without paying 100 gold, but Gill has not confirmed such a trade.
classification.action_basis: Gill only named the dragon as the needed work in reply to Dunk's question; no explicit agreement to exchange the mule for it was made.

facts.resource_subject: Killing the dragon as the work Dunk could trade for Shamus

facts.text: Acquire the mithril chain shirt Warwick the smith displays in his shop.
facts.uncertain_reason: Dunk only heard about the shirt from Farmer Gill; no party member has said they want it.

facts.text: Farmer Gill says Warwick always refuses to sell the mithril chain shirt he displays.

classification.scope_basis: Gill describes Warwick's refusal as habitual ('always refuses'), a standing condition rather than a single encounter.

facts.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley and collect Quinn's 100 gold.
Quinn's plan: he brings up bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering ale to stage a fake shipment.

classification.support_basis: Carrying out the staged delivery is the agreed way of doing the job Quinn will pay for, though how it hurts Bentley was not spelled out.
classification.action_basis: Quinn proposed the plan, will supply the bottles, and Sir Phidipaldi agreed to perform the delivery.

facts.text: What empties or knocks over Quinn's stock every night? Quinn blames Bentley.

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn explicitly describes a recurring nightly loss of a fully stocked bar, with glasses half empty or knocked over, and his blame of Bentley rests only on Bentley's popularity.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden culprit and their means behind a recurring pattern.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Identifying the true culprit could overturn Quinn's accusation and change the party's view of the revenge job.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: A night watch at the Golden Egg or questioning townsfolk could plausibly uncover the culprit.
